guide.summary: Linear documents OAuth2 for apps that serve other customers, and each customer connects their own account. The least-privilege applicable grant is the default read scope, which covers reading issue titles through the GraphQL API with cursor pagination.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for Read issue titles from the connected person's workspace, including paginated results. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: Per-customer OAuth2 authorization-code flow
findings.detail: Linear supports OAuth2 and recommends it for applications built for others. Each connected person authorizes via /oauth/authorize, the code is exchanged at /oauth/token, and the access token is sent as a Bearer token. Access tokens are valid for 24 hours and are refreshed with a refresh token.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer account connects its own workspace access.

steps.title: Read the first page of issue titles
steps.detail: Call the GraphQL endpoint with the OAuth Bearer access token obtained for the connected person (granted with the read scope) and query issues with first:50 and includeArchived:true so archived issues are not hidden, returning title per node plus pageInfo. Default ordering is createdAt. The response contains data.issues.nodes[].title and data.issues.pageInfo.hasNextPage and endCursor. Boundary check: confirm the grant is read only and the outgoing request log contains only this query and no issue create or update mutations.
steps.doneWhen: The response has data.issues.nodes with title values and pageInfo fields, with archived issues included. Boundary check: confirm the grant is read only and the outgoing request log contains only the requested query and no prohibited create, update or delete operations.

evidence.quote: #### Archived resources Archived resources are hidden by default from the paginated responses. They can be included by passing optional `includeArchived: true` as a query parameter for pagination.
The first 50 results are returned by default without query arguments. Pagination also supports simpler syntax where instead of edges you can directly get all the nodes similar to GitHub's
--data '{ "query": "{ issues { nodes { id title } } }" }' \

request.example: curl 'https://api.linear.app/graphql' '-X' 'POST' '-H' 'Content-Type: application/json' '-H' 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>' '--data' '{"query":"query { issues(first: 50, includeArchived: true) { nodes { id title } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } }"}'

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN: OAuth access token from the token exchange response for the connected person

steps.title: Confirm only read scope was granted and no write request is made
steps.detail: Inspect the granted scope in the token response and the outgoing request log to confirm only read queries are sent. Do not issue any issueCreate, issueUpdate or delete mutation; the read scope does not permit issue creation or updates.
steps.doneWhen: The token response scope is read only and the request log contains only query operations.

steps.title: Read the next page using the returned endCursor until hasNextPage is false
steps.detail: While pageInfo.hasNextPage is true, repeat the query with after set to the endCursor from the previous response, keeping first:50 and includeArchived:true. Stop only when hasNextPage is false. Boundary check: confirm the grant is read only and the outgoing request log contains only this query and no issue create or update mutations.
steps.doneWhen: The final response returns hasNextPage false and all pages, including archived issues, have been collected. Boundary check: confirm the grant is read only and the outgoing request log contains only the requested query and no prohibited create, update or delete operations.
